home.heroLede: ED Robotics is a club that inspires and builds the innovators of tomorrow — run by upper secondary students at Erik Dahlberg Upper Secondary School in Jönköping.
home.bulletinP1: ED Robotics represented Sweden at the FIRST Robotics Competition in Orlando, Florida – the world's largest robotics competition for young engineers. After an eventful week on the field, the whole team is safely back home.
home.bulletinP2: Read the full recap: from last-minute robot builds to climbing robots and a visit to the Kennedy Space Center.
home.bulletinThanks: Thank you to everyone who made the trip possible! ❤️
home.card1Body: What do we do, and where do we do it? Read about our projects, competitions, and everyday life in the workshop.
home.card2Body: In 2024 we traveled to Albany, NY to compete in the First Robotics Competition.
home.card3Body: We offer a wide range of sponsorship packages for companies who want to support young engineers.
home.seasonBody: In 2024 we were the only team from Sweden to compete in the First Robotics Competition. How did it go? Watch the whole journey in our Season Recap.
home.challengeBody: If you're into robotics, engineering, or simply a challenge – join us! Follow our projects and be part of the team when we compete in RoboCup and the FIRST Robotics Competition in the USA.

meta.title: About us | ED Robotics
meta.description: Get to know ED Robotics — who we are, what we do, and where we meet.

about.who1: ED Robotics is a robotics club based at Erik Dahlberg Upper Secondary School in Jönköping. Our goal isn't just to give ED's students the chance to take part in exciting, hands-on robotics projects — it's to build a warm and successful community of future engineers.
about.who2: ED Robotics was founded in 2022, and we currently work on several independent robotics projects, primarily RoboCup and FRC. Help us build robots that walk, roll, swim, fly, play football, and even navigate Mars!
about.what1: Members get the chance to make a real impact on a complex, multidisciplinary, multi-stage engineering project at a level most upper secondary students never encounter. As a member, you'll gain experience in milling, 3D printing, microcontrollers, electronics, coding languages, hardware–software integration, algorithms, and much more.
about.what2: No prior experience with robotics is required, but a willingness to learn and put in the time is. Want to build some cool robots and have fun while you're at it? Join us!
about.frcBody: FIRST Robotics Competition combines the excitement of sport with the rigor of science and technology – often called "the ultimate sport for the mind". Under strict rules, limited resources, and tight deadlines, teams are challenged to raise funds, design a team "brand", hone teamwork skills, and build and program industrial-sized robots to play a difficult field game against like-minded competitors. Volunteer professional mentors lend their time and talent to guide every team.
about.robocupBody: RoboCup Junior is a project-oriented robotics competition for students up to age 19, focused on creating an environment where students grow by expanding their knowledge, sparking their curiosity, and becoming comfortable with technology. The competition has three branches — Soccer, Rescue, and OnStage — each built around collaborative problem-solving for creative young minds with a range of interests and skills.

partners.intro: Building robots is fun, but equipment and materials aren't cheap, and as we grow, so do our running costs. Supporting our club doesn't just expose your products and mission to Erik Dahlberg's students and the public — it also creates meaningful educational and professional opportunities for our future engineers.
